name: Perl
title: Perl (5.42)

type.text: **TIMTOWTDI**: "There's More Than One Way To Do It" creates inconsistency
**Context-sensitive**: Same code behaves differently in scalar/list context
**Moose**: Object system add-on provides types, not core
**A method call resolves on the run-time object**: `$obj->method` looks the name up in the object's class when the call runs, so a rename breaks a caller only at run time
**Regular expressions**: Write-only code, couples understanding to expertise

construction.text: **Core class syntax is experimental**: `use feature 'class'` provides a core object system, but the implementation is still experimental, so a project cannot rely on it
**Moose/Moo**: Modern OOP libraries improve this significantly
**Collection order is unpinned**: the documentation states hash order is not the source's, and Perl randomizes it per process to catch the agreement
**One value, many names**: references are first-class, and the language's containers reach one structure through names the declaration does not count

error.text: **Return undef**: Many functions return `undef` on error, silent failures
**$!**: Global error variable couples error state
**Signatures declare parameters only**: A sub's signature does not state the errors it may raise, so the failure channel is invisible at the call
**A fault ends the program**: a thread die ends the process (documented in the threading manual); eval recovers frames, not units

concurrency.text: **No modern concurrency**: No async/await, no actors
**A thread is an interpreter thread**: Each one reserves an operating-system thread, so the program pays per task

platform.text: **No company owns the language**: Perl 5 is released by the Perl 5 Porters under the Artistic License and the GNU General Public License, and no vendor controls it
**The interpreter is portable**: The same C source builds on Linux, macOS, the BSDs, Windows through Strawberry Perl, and OpenVMS
**CPAN is vendor-neutral**: The archive is mirrored worldwide and serves any Perl distribution, not one vendor's package service
**A base interpreter ships with most Unix systems**: Many Linux distributions and the BSDs install `perl` as part of the base system, so a script needs no extra platform

performance.text: **Interpreted**: Slower than compiled, and the reference interpreter has no JIT
**Regex engine**: Very fast for text processing
**Memory usage**: Higher than C, lower than Ruby/Python

ecosystem.text: **Aging**: Fewer new modules than modern ecosystems
**IDE support**: Limited compared to modern languages
**An XS module binds to a Perl build**: the C code compiles against one Perl's headers and build flags [@perlModInstall]

**Stored data crosses on a published promise**: a Storable header carries the file format version, and a reading Storable defers croaking until it meets a data type it does not recognize [@perlStorable]

domain.text: **Excellent for text processing**: Regex, sed/awk replacement
**Web declining**: CGI era passed, PSGI exists

learning.text: **Write-only code**: Hard to read others' code

security.text: **Eval risks**: Code injection if used carelessly

governance.text: **Semantics rest on the implementation**: the documentation describes what perl does, and no published conformance suite exists for an independent implementation

tradeoffs: **Regexes are woven into the grammar**: Pattern matching is syntax rather than a library, which makes text handling concise and the language hard to read — a syntax decision, not a coupling mechanism
**Sigils prefix every name**: The leading `$`, `@`, or `%` encodes the noun in the identifier, a readability trade expressed in the name rather than in a type system
**Scalars carry both a number and a string**: The dual-valued scalar is why `==` and `eq` are separate operators, a convenience whose cost falls on every comparison

**Backward compatibility is the default**: Decades of behaviour remain in the language, and `use strict` and `use warnings` recover discipline one file at a time — a compatibility cost, not a forced dependency
**The successor was released as another language**: Raku was developed separately from Perl 5, so Perl 5 continues on its own line — a project decision, not a coupling
verdict: Perl is era before static analysis was common. TIMTOWTDI creates inconsistent coupling patterns. Context sensitivity couples behavior to call site. Implicit $_ creates hidden dependencies. Main strength: CPAN ecosystem, regex power, system administration tasks. Main weakness: "write-only" code couples maintenance to original author's knowledge.

energy.text: Interpreted by default: the slowest class in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Moderate training data: models write it competently, with measurable language-specific weakness [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: A distribution is built against the local Perl at install time
XS code compiles against one Perl build, and a shipped binary binds to that build

data_formats.note: Perl publishes the promise for Storable images: the header carries the file format version, the version number increments only when additional features that would confuse older versions of the module are added, and a reading Storable defers croaking until it meets a data type it does not recognize, so a file from a newer release opens on the current one
